title: Mission 08: The Investigation
story: Security flagged the department: someone has been accessing the system at strange hours. The evidence is buried across thousands of log lines and a directory of case files. You cannot read it all - but grep can. Patterns are your flashlight; the needle never stood a chance.

badge.name: The Investigation: Case Closed
badge.desc: Mastered grep by pulling a suspect out of thousands of log lines with patterns alone.

tasks.brief: Read BRIEFING8.txt in your department directory. Start broad: save every line of casework/auth.log containing the word FAILED to casework/failed.txt.

checks.fail: failed.txt must contain exactly the auth.log lines containing FAILED, in original order.

tasks.brief: The attacker mixes case to dodge filters: Denied, DENIED, denied. Save every line of auth.log with the word denied IN ANY CASE to casework/denied.txt.

checks.fail: denied.txt must catch denied in EVERY case combination (grep has a case-insensitive option).

tasks.brief: How many auth.log lines mention the suspect '$MISSION_SUSPECT'? Do not count by hand: grep can count matching lines itself. Just the number goes in casework/suspectcount.txt.

checks.fail: suspectcount.txt must contain just the number of auth.log lines mentioning the suspect (grep has a count option).

tasks.brief: Produce the CLEAN log: every auth.log line that does NOT contain FAILED, to casework/clean.txt (grep can invert a match).

checks.fail: clean.txt must be every line WITHOUT the word FAILED (invert the match).

tasks.brief: The prosecutor needs positions: every ROOT-escalation line WITH its line number, exactly as grep prints them, to casework/rootlines.txt (pattern: 'escalation to root').

checks.fail: rootlines.txt must be grep's line-numbered output for 'escalation to root' (a one-letter option prefixes numbers).

tasks.brief: Searching 'ops' drowns you in 'gridops' and 'devops' noise. Save only lines where ops stands as a WHOLE WORD to casework/opsword.txt (grep can anchor on word boundaries).

checks.fail: opsword.txt must match ops only as a whole word - gridops and devops lines stay out.

tasks.brief: The suspect left traces beyond the log. Search the ENTIRE casework/files directory recursively for '$MISSION_SUSPECT' and save grep's output (with filenames, as recursive grep prints) to casework/traces.txt.

checks.fail: traces.txt must be recursive grep output over casework/files (run it FROM the casework directory against the relative name files, so the filename prefixes match).

tasks.brief: The strange hours: entries between 02:00 and 04:59 AM. One regex catches them all: save auth.log lines matching times 02:, 03: or 04: at the timestamp position to casework/nighthours.txt using a character-class pattern (like [0X-Y] inside your regex).

checks.fail: nighthours.txt must catch every 02:xx, 03:xx and 04:xx entry with one pattern (a character class like 0[2-4] does it).
auth.log was modified. Evidence is read-only; the case would be thrown out.

tasks.brief: BONUS: the warrant lists FILES, not lines. Save just the NAMES of the files under casework/files that mention the suspect (one per line, as grep's files-with-matches option prints them, run from casework/) to casework/warrant.txt.

checks.fail: warrant.txt must be just the matching filenames (grep has a files-with-matches option; run it from casework/ against files).
